signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.50, holding just below the 160.00 threshold where intervention risk previously escalated. Crude prices jumped 2.55% following headlines of a US-Iran ceasefire at a standstill, introducing a fresh geopolitical risk premium. Despite the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage supporting the pair, the options market is aggressively hedging for a reversal. The 25d risk reversal at -2.06 (Saxo, 1M tenor) marks a strong put skew, indicating that institutional desks are paying a premium for USD/JPY downside protection. This divergence between carry-driven spot and defensive options pricing suggests the market is bracing for an intervention or a geopolitical volatility spike. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry dominance remains intact until a sustained break above 160.00 or a VIX spike toward 25. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias 1.0% vs Fed 3.75%. Risk: Confirmed BoJ/MoF intervention triggers a disorderly unwind of crowded spec shorts.

signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/JPY displays a G10 bilateral theme with a 1.140% performance spread between the weekly leader and laggard. NZD is the G10 leader with a +0.649% average (n=4 pairs), supported by its RBNZ hiking regime and a positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +6.2. JPY remains the laggard, down -0.491% on average (n=7 pairs), as its accommodative real rate of -0.70% continues to facilitate carry-funding despite verbal intervention warnings. While NZD/USD trades at 0.5904 above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, the spec positioning in NZD remains at a 52-week low with a COT LF net of -34,031 (pctl 2). RBNZ holds at 2.5%. Trade bias: Long NZD/JPY; outperformance spread favors the RBNZ-BoJ policy divergence. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias intact. Risk: JPY safe-haven demand revives on further Middle East escalation, compressing the carry spread.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + Technical Cluster
signals.text: AUD/USD is testing 0.7111, positioned firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.703/0.699/0.694) in a bullish technical configuration. Retail sentiment has reached an extreme 85% short, fading the +0.67% weekly rally in direct opposition to institutional flows. COT data shows Leveraged Funds are net long +45,727 (pctl 75), with a WoW delta of +7,737 as specs continue to chase the AUD carry premium. The 73bp OIS carry advantage (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.62%) provides structural support for the pair while US data continues to disappoint (ESI -13.8). This institutional-retail divergence typically precedes a capitulation move by retail traders if price holds above the SMA cluster. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; supported by carry and retail contrarian signals. Catalyst: Jackson Hole symposium later this week. Risk: US data surprises to the upside, reviving Fed hike odds and flattening the carry advantage.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Real Rate Spread
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1583, showing limited intraday volatility despite a 149bp 10Y yield deficit against the US. The options market is pricing in significant tail risk, with 1M IV at 7.1% vs a 30-day realized volatility (HV30) of 4.2%, resulting in an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +2.9%. While the nominal carry spread of +135bp (Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.4%) favors the USD, the real policy rate differential is much tighter at 1.41% (USD +1.51% vs EUR +0.10%). Speculative positioning remains bearish with EUR LF net at -77,671 (pctl 8, z -2.17), but the negative Economic Surprise Index for USD (-13.8) is limiting greenback upside. Trade bias: Neutral/Range EUR/USD; high vol premium makes directional conviction expensive. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias present. Risk: EUR/USD breaks 1.1634 (SMA200), triggering a technical short-squeeze in the crowded spec short.
